issue: Understand data flow from API to database

observations.detail: POST /api/products traverses 9 layers: Rate Limiter → Auth Middleware (JWT) → Route Handler → Validation → Business Logic (enrichment, slug, timestamps) → ORM/Database (INSERT INTO products) → Cache (invalidation of list/count/search keys) → Event Emission (product.created webhook) → Response (201 Created with full Product entity). Each layer has distinct error responses following the standard { error: { code, message } } format.

Source code is distributed across feature branches, not on master. Route definitions in feature/openapi-spec-generation, rate limiting in feature/rate-limiting-middleware, cache store in fix/cache-race-condition, webhook retry in feature/webhook-retry-exponential-backoff. Master branch is documentation-only. Architecture documentation must cross-reference these branches.

Created the architecture doc as docs/guides/api-data-flow-architecture.md (alongside existing guides) rather than a top-level docs/architecture.md. This follows the existing docs structure where technical deep-dives live in guides/. Included both Mermaid and ASCII diagrams for accessibility across rendering environments.

The codebase has grown with implementation spread across branches but documentation is centralized on master. For investigations and architecture docs, the deliverable is always a documentation artifact on master, not code changes. This matches the routing.md rule: Investigations → Architect → documentation output.

The cache store uses per-key mutex locking (KeyLock class) with version stamping for optimistic concurrency. On product mutations (POST/PUT/DELETE), the cache invalidates list/count/search keys rather than updating them. Cache failures are non-fatal and don't propagate to API responses.

Included microservices migration notes in the architecture doc since the issue specifically mentioned planning for microservices migration. Recommended extraction order: Auth Service (stateless) → Event Bus (async) → Product Service (core domain) → Cache (shared infra). This provides actionable guidance beyond just documenting current state.
